name: Panoptic V1.1
rootCause: A Cantina security researcher disclosed a critical vulnerability on August 25, 2025 in Panoptic's position fingerprint calculation algorithm. The protocol's position fingerprinting had unknowingly implemented a variant of XHASH — a cryptographic construction previously identified as insecure in academic literature — that relied on XOR operations in a manner that reduced hash collision resistance to polynomial time. This flaw allowed an attacker to spoof position ownership by crafting colliding TokenId hashes, enabling unauthorized claims over positions they did not hold and threatening approximately $5M in user funds. Weaknesses in position list validation and sanity checks that could have hinted at the issue were surfaced in Panoptic's April 2024 Code4rena audit but neither report fully described the exploit path. Upon disclosure, Panoptic coordinated a white-hat rescue operation with Cantina and Seal911, proactively securing approximately $400K in at-risk funds before any malicious actor could exploit the gap; no user funds were ultimately lost, and the disclosing researcher received a $250K bounty. Attack Tx: 0x67a45dfe5ff4b190058674d7c791bbdc48e889f319f937c24fa13a5f9093f088 Analysis: Panoptic — Security disclosure and rescue announcement

Panoptic V1.1 was exposed to a severe position fingerprinting vulnerability that could have allowed an attacker to drain all funds from deployed pools. The flaw was detected before malicious exploitation, enabling a coordinated whitehat rescue and voluntary withdrawals, resulting in no user losses. Over $4M in at-risk assets was secured and redistributed via a Merkle-root mechanism. The protocol used XOR aggregation of Keccak256 hashes to fingerprint user position lists for collateral/debt verification.
